data.rationale: parse_identityinfo_header() calls parse_identityinfo(body.s, body.s + body.len + 1, ...) at lines 347-349, passing an end pointer one byte beyond the header body. The body range [body.s, body.s+body.len) is what the core parser set in msg_parser.c (hdr->body.len = tmp - hdr->body.s), so the +1 makes the state-machine loop at parse_identityinfo.c:53 ('for(p = buffer; p < end; p++)') dereference *p at p == body.s+body.len, a byte outside the body. Reachability: the fuzz target misc/fuzz/fuzz_parse_msg.c calls parse_msg() on the raw input then parse_identityinfo_header(&orig_inv) at line 60. Since the fuzzer input buffer is heap-allocated by libFuzzer, an Identity-Info header ending exactly at the end of the message (e.g. last header with no trailing CRLF beyond body) makes body.s+body.len the end of the heap buffer, and reading the extra byte triggers a heap-buffer-overflow READ. The root cause is the +1 in the end-pointer computation in parse_identityinfo_header.
